Subject: Private deploy — topology & isolation artefacts (initial)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for agreeing to look over the private VPC topology for our planned Redwood private deployment. Attached are two files: a topology PDF (aperture-vpc-topology-v1.pdf) and a short spreadsheet mapping tenants to VLANs and peering relationships (aperture-control-data-segmentation.xlsx).

High level asks from our security/compliance team:
- Verify that the control plane (management API, provisioning, k8s control plane) is logically and network-wise isolated from customer data plane traffic.
- Confirm egress proofing (how model telemetry/audit logs leave our network, and where KMS calls terminate).
- Provide recommended collars for multi-tenant isolation (namespace-level plus host-level), and whether an additional NAT/egress proxy is required for our HA setup.

We'd like to capture a short "isolation proof" note we can put in our SOC 2 evidence pack. Can you let us know whether a 30–45 minute review today or tomorrow works? We're on Pacific time.

Attachments: aperture-vpc-topology-v1.pdf, aperture-control-data-segmentation.xlsx

Thanks,

Samira —

Appreciate the artifacts. We can do a quick review today at 1:00pm PT; if that doesn't work we'll do 10:00am PT tomorrow. I'll sketch an isolation proof during the call and follow up with a short one-page summary you can include in SOC 2 evidence.

Preliminary notes after a quick scan:
- Control plane endpoints should be placed in a management VPC with private peering to the customer VPCs (no public-facing control endpoints).
- Data plane (model-serving pods/nodes) must be in tenant-dedicated subnets with strict security groups and host-level node isolation (we recommend gVisor or host-level seccomp profiles for additional defense-in-depth).
- KMS calls: prefer customer-managed KMS via a VPC endpoint (or HSM proxy) — we'll note recommended LDAP/KMS flows in the summary.

I'll include Marissa and Jonas on the call to capture operational/handoff items. Meeting invite incoming.

—Kimberly

Subject: Re: Private deploy — topology & isolation artefacts (internal ops notes)

Kimberly / Jonas —

Quick internal notes ahead of the call (I'll add these to the review doc during the call):
1) Control plane topology
   - API/control plane in a dedicated management VPC, peered to tenant VPCs via private VPC peering or Transit Gateway depending on scale. No public ingress to kube-api; access exclusively via bastion/jump and RBAC.
   - Control plane HA: active/standby across AZs with floating peering endpoints; recommend mutual TLS between Redwood control plane components and customer-managed endpoints.
2) Data plane segregation
   - Tenant pods scheduled on tenant-labeled node pools. NetworkPolicy enforces namespace-to-namespace restrictions. For stricter separation add node affinity + separate subnets and route tables.
   - Consider eBPF-based observability instead of host-level promiscuous flows to avoid cross-tenant leakage.
3) Egress and telemetry
   - Audit logs: push to a customer-owned logging bucket via private endpoint. Telemetry metrics can be sampled and proxied via a dedicated egress proxy (authn + rate-limit).
   - KMS/HSM: recommend using a dedicated KMS VPC endpoint (customer-managed) or an HSM appliance behind an internal proxy; do NOT use public KMS endpoints for secret material in this deployment.
4) Evidence / artifacts for SOC2
   - We'll produce a short 1-page isolation proof: diagram, access controls, egress flow, KMS call trace, and a list of audit log S3 prefixes + retention.

Attachments I plan to send after the call: 1) Proposed isolation proof (PDF) 2) Host-level node labeling and admission control snippet (yaml).

If Jonas can capture the inbound/outbound firewall rules and the intended BGP egress behavior, we can include those in the evidence set.

—Marissa
